# Adjudication Task — Chapter 549

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃549화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 수천 명의 군단을 이끄는 장군이 아니다.
  6|
  7|화룡각의 구성원은 나를 포함한다 해도 고작 여섯 명.
  8|
  9|모두가 한자리에 모이는 데에는 한 식경이면 충분했다.
 10|
 11|“모두 주목.”
 12|
 13|인사도, 존칭도 생략한 채 불쑥 꺼낸 한마디에 심상치 않은 기류를 느낀 다섯 사람의 시선이 집중된다.
 14|
 15|아직 이들을 부르러 갔던 혁무진조차 전후 사정을 제대로 알지 못하는 상황.
 16|
 17|의문이 서린 얼굴들을 차례대로 응시한 나는 천천히 입술을 뗐다.
 18|
 19|“바로 본론부터 들어가자면…… 한 가지 임무를 받았다.”
 20|
 21|뺄 것도, 더할 것도 없었다.
 22|
 23|나는 있는 그대로를 설명해 주었고, 간단한 브리핑은 일각도 채 흐르기 전에 끝났다.
 24|
 25|그리고 모두가 약속이라도 한 것처럼 입을 다문 채 생각에 잠겨 있던 그때, 한 사람이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“그러니까.”
 28|
 29|침착한 목소리의 주인은 익히 아는 얼굴이었다.
 30|
 31|흑룡마문(黑龍魔門)의 소문주, 사마표가 나를 응시하며 말을 이었다.
 32|
 33|“남만으로 향한다. 이거로군.”
 34|
 35|나는 고개를 끄덕였다. 가벼운 정정과 함께.
 36|
 37|“정확히는 남만이 아니라, 남만야수궁(南蠻野獸宮)이지.”
 38|
 39|남만야수궁. 영물과 독물을 비롯하여 수많은 동물들을 길들이고, 그것들의 움직임을 본 따 무공을 수련한다는 신비의 문파.
 40|
 41|동물 보호 협회인지 학대 집단인지는 잘 모르겠지만, 적어도 한 가지는 확실하다.
 42|
 43|‘홍란. 아니, 남천마후(南天魔后)가 군침을 흘릴 만한 장소라는 거.’
 44|
 45|두 번째 ‘균열’이 일어난다는 가정하에, 암천 입장에서는 남만야수궁만큼 적격인 곳을 찾기도 힘들다.
 46|
 47|그야말로 동물의 왕국이요, 천하에서 가장 많은 영물과 독물들이 득실거리는 곳이니까.
 48|
 49|유엽도(柳葉刀) 한 자루를 품에 안고 이야기를 듣던 송일섬이 중얼거렸다.
 50|
 51|“고생길이 훤하군.”
 52|
 53|녀석이 이런 말을 하는 데에는 충분한 이유가 있었다.
 54|
 55|남만야수궁이 자리 잡은 남만은 중원에서 운남(雲南)이라고도 불리는 곳.
 56|
 57|위치상으로는 사천의 바로 아래에 붙어 있으며 귀주, 광서와 땅을 맞대고 있다.
 58|
 59|이렇게 들으면 단지 거리가 멀 뿐, 아무런 문제도 없어 보이지만…….
 60|
 61|‘문제는, 남만 자체의 지리와 기후가 엄청나게 지랄 맞다는 거지.’
 62|
 63|남만에는 푹푹 찌는 열대 기후에 밀림이 끝도 없이 늘어져 있다고 했다.
 64|
 65|잘 정비된 가도(街道)는 눈을 씻고 찾아봐도 없고 대신 잘 큰 맹수나 독충이 인간을 밥차 취급하는, 실로 거지 같은 동네라 할 수 있었다.
 66|
 67|‘얼추 들은 것만 해도 이 정도인데…….’
 68|
 69|실제로는 어느 정도일지 쉽게 짐작이 가지 않는다.
 70|
 71|천하를 그려 넣은 지도에도 어엿하게 들어간 남만이 왜 새외(塞外) 취급받는지 어렴풋이 알 것 같기도 했다.
 72|
 73|‘사실 현대적 관점에서 보면 외국이 맞긴 하지.’
 74|
 75|운남이 현대에서는 베트남과 미얀마던가. 그쯤 어딘가에 있을 텐데 세계지리 시간에 잠만 처자느라 기억이 가물가물하다.
 76|
 77|기억을 되짚고 있던 그때 혁무진이 손을 번쩍 치켜들었다.
 78|
 79|“저기, 조장님. 질문이 있는데요.”
 80|
 81|“말해.”
 82|
 83|“진짜 갑니까?”
 84|
 85|“그럼 가짜로 가냐?”
 86|
 87|“그, 너무 위험할 것 같은데요.”
 88|
 89|“뭐 어때. 지금까지도 항상 위험했는데.”
 90|
 91|“……당연하게 말씀하시니까 할 말이 없네요.”
 92|
 93|“할 말 없으면 입 다물고 짐이나 싸.”
 94|
 95|“언제 출발하는데요?”
 96|
 97|“아, 내가 말 안 했나?”
 98|
 99|중요한 걸 깜빡했군.
100|
101|다른 사람들도 목적지와 그 이유에 대해 집중하느라 미처 생각하지 못한 것이 분명했다.
102|
103|한 사람, 한 사람을 차례차례 바라본 나는 한 마디를 툭 내뱉었다.
104|
105|“오늘 당장.”
106|
107|“……!”
108|
109|“……!”
110|
111|작은 파문이 순식간에 번져 나간다. 그중에서도 특히 혁무진과, 호거아(虎巨兒) 태산이 그랬다.
112|
113|“농담이시죠?”
114|
115|“지금 같은 상황에 농담할 것 같냐?”
116|
117|“말도 안 돼. 당장 챙겨야 할 옷이나 물자는요?”
118|
119|“말 돼. 우리가 언제부터 의식주 철저하게 따졌다고. 그냥 벽곡단이나 챙겨.”
120|
121|후욱, 훅!
122|
123|깜짝이야. 열양지기인가.
124|
125|놀라울 만큼 뜨거운 콧김을 뿜어낸 태산이 자리에서 벌떡 일어나며 외쳤다.
126|
127|“안 된다! 태산이! 오늘 저녁! 고기 먹기로 했다!”
128|
129|“고기? 고기 좋지.”
130|
131|나는 혁무진을 향해 한 마디를 덧붙였다.
132|
133|“들었지? 육포도 챙겨라.”
134|
135|“육포! 맛없다!”
136|
137|“……그냥 닥치고 아무거나 처먹어.”
138|
139|젓가락도 뜯어 먹게 생긴 놈이 입맛 까다로운 것 보소.
140|
141|내 시선에 담긴 뜻을 알아차린 사마표가 어깨를 으쓱하며 입을 열었다.
142|
143|“태산. 네 이 녀석.”
144|
145|“주, 주군.”
146|
147|“언제까지 그리 천방지축으로 굴 테냐. 만약 계속 생떼를 쓴다면…….”
148|
149|“태산이. 안 그러겠다. 용서해 줘라. 주군.”
150|
151|저 덩치 큰 놈이 얼마나 기가 죽었는지, 나도 모르게 미안한 마음이 들 정도다.
152|
153|앞으로 태산에 관한 일은 사마표에게 맡겨야겠다고 생각한 나는 미간을 찌푸리고 있는 송일섬에게 시선을 돌렸다.
154|
155|“왜. 너도 불만 있냐?”
156|
157|“물론. 다른 곳도 아니고 남만이니까.”
158|
159|작게 혀를 찬 송일섬이 말을 이었다.
160|
161|“하지만 없는 것으로 치지. 애석하게도 이미 선금을 두둑이 받아 버렸거든. 열 배나 되는 위약금을 지불할 자신도 없고.”
162|
163|“생각했던 것보다 훨씬 깔끔한데. 마음에 들어.”
164|
165|“한 번 맺은 계약은 지킨다. 그러지 않았다면 추혼객(追魂客)이라는 이름도 없었어.”
166|
167|강한 신념과 자부심이 느껴지는 한 마디를 툭 내뱉은 송일섬이 덤덤하게 말을 이었다.
168|
169|“물론 최종 결정은 내가 아니라 고용주가 하는 거고. 그렇지 않소?”
170|
171|당연하게도 마지막 물음은 내게 던진 것이 아니다.
172|
173|처음부터 지금까지, 줄곧 아무 말 없이 어떤 생각에 잠겨 있던 한 사람, 은비화(隱匕花) 주화란이 마침내 입을 열었다.
174|
175|“제가 어떤 대답을 할지. 이미 알고 있을 것 같은데요. 아닌가요?”
176|
177|귓가를 파고드는 나긋하면서도 맑은 목소리에, 나는 피식 웃었고 송일섬은 작게 한숨을 내쉬었다.
178|
179|“내 이럴 줄 알았지. 제기랄, 남만이라니.”
180|
181|“계약 내용을 다시 상기시켜 드릴 필요는 없을 거라 믿어요. 송 대협.”
182|
183|앓는 소리를 흘리는 송일섬을 뒤로한 주화란이 나를 물끄러미 응시했다.
184|
185|신비한 빛을 띤 검푸른 눈동자에 내 얼굴이 비친다. 이렇게 가까이서 보니까 꼭…….
186|
187|“진 대협?”
188|
189|“아, 네.”
190|
191|방금 뭐였지. 잠깐 졸았나.
192|
193|주화란의 부름에 정신을 차린 나는 내심 중얼거렸다.
194|
195|‘안 되지. 안 돼.’
196|
197|벌써부터 이러면 곤란하다. 앞으로의 일을 생각하면 언제나 냉정한 상태에서 상황에 임해야 했다.
198|
199|몇 번이고 뇌까리며 마음을 다잡은 나는 최대한 침착한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
200|
201|“잘됐네요. 안 그래도 물어볼 것이 있었습니다. 다름이 아니라…….”
202|
203|말을 이으려던 그때였다.
204|
205|“남만으로 향하는 가장 빠른 길과 필요한 것에 대해서겠죠? 좋아요.”
206|
207|“예?”
208|
209|“왜요? 제 생각이 틀렸나요?”
210|
211|“아뇨. 그게 아니라.”
212|
213|오히려 그 반대다. 너무 정확해서 깜짝 놀랐다.
214|
215|뭐야, 이거. 설마 독심술이라도 익힌 건가? 관심법. 뭐 그런 거야?
216|
217|말문이 막힌 채 눈을 깜빡이는 나를 향해, 주화란이 싱긋 웃어 보였다.
218|
219|“놀라실 것 없어요. 아까부터 제가 할 수 있는 일을 생각하고 있었으니까.”
220|
221|“아.”
222|
223|“저도 정식으로 화룡각의 일원이 되었으니, 지난번에 말씀드렸던 것처럼 한 사람 몫을 해내야겠죠.”
224|
225|톡. 톡톡.
226|
227|그녀 역시 한 사람의 검수(劍手)라는 것을 알려 주듯, 새하얗지만 거친 손가락이 일정한 속도로 탁자 위를 두드린다.
228|
229|그리고 이어 흘러나오는 목소리.
230|
231|“우선 진 대협께서도 말씀하셨듯이, 물자는 최소한으로 하는 것이 좋겠네요. 의복은 필요 없고, 식량도 건량으로 이틀 치면 충분해요.”
232|
233|“건량이라니! 그것만은 제발! 태산이 죽는다!”
234|
235|태산의 통곡에 주화란이 재빨리 덧붙였다.
236|
237|“물론 육포도요.”
238|
239|“저 새끼 보호자 뭐 하냐. 아, 주 소저는 계속 말씀하세요.”
240|
241|“네. 그럼…….”
242|
243|골칫덩이를 치워 버린 주화란은 막힘 없이 말을 이어 갔다.
244|
245|필요한 물품부터 남만으로 향하는 가장 빠른 길까지.
246|
247|다행히도 그녀는 수년 전 남만에 표행을 갔던 경험이 있었고, 조부인 표왕이 남긴 기록을 통해 곳곳의 지형과 숨겨진 길 역시 알고 있었다.
248|
249|코흘리개 시절부터 천하를 방랑하는 낭인의 삶을 살았던 송일섬조차 놀라움을 표할 정도였다.
250|
251|“그런 길이 있었단 말이오?”
252|
253|주화란이 자신 있게 고개를 끄덕였다.
254|
255|“물론이에요. 할아버님의 기록에 따르면 확실해요.”
256|
257|“나 역시 그곳에 일 년 정도 머물렀던 적이 있소. 하지만 내가 알기로는…….”
258|
259|“할아버님의 기록에 따르면 확실해요.”
260|
261|“아니, 그건 아는데. 내 말은.”
262|
263|“할아버님. 기록.”
264|
265|“이보시오. 내 말도 좀.”
266|
267|“표왕.”
268|
269|“……믿겠소. 믿을 테니까 계속하시오.”
270|
271|표왕이 누구인가. 자그마치 십만의 마교도가 천하를 뒤덮은 와중에도 그 전설적인 만리행을 성공시킨 레전드 중의 레전드.
272|
273|바로 그 P왕의 의지를 이은 주 P. 화란은 물 만난 고잉메리호처럼 막힘 없이 나아갔고, 불과 한 식경이 지나기도 전에 남만으로 향하는 모든 경로 계획을 수립하는 기염을 토했다.
274|
275|“후, 우선은 여기까지네요. 질문 있으신 분?”
276|
277|후웅!
278|
279|트롤의 것으로 의심될 만큼 굵은 팔이 번쩍 솟구쳤다.
280|
281|“네, 뭐든 물어보세요.”
282|
283|호거라 태산이 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
284|
285|“태산이. 육포 이후로 아무것도 이해 못 했다.”
286|
287|“…….”
288|
289|“…….”
290|
291|어떤 새끼가 노키즈존에 애를 데려왔냐.
292|
293|나는 날카로운 눈빛으로 한 사람을 쏘아보았다.
294|
295|“야, 보호자.”
296|
297|“미안하군.”
298|
299|텁.
300|
301|“읍. 읍!”
302|
303|내 일갈에 즉각 태산의 입을 틀어막은 사마표가 주화란을 향해 고개를 까딱였다.
304|
305|“미안하오.”
306|
307|“……괜찮아요.”
308|
309|말투는 덤덤하지만, 가라앉은 목소리만큼은 숨길 수 없다. 상황이 상황인 만큼 어쩔 수 없는 일일 것이다.
310|
311|아니, 당연한 일이지.
312|

With the interruption dealt with, Ju Hwaran continued without a pause. She covered everything from the supplies we’d need to the fastest route to Nanman.

[P108]
Fortunately, she had traveled there on an escort assignment several years ago. She also knew the terrain and hidden roads in various places from the records her grandfather, the Escort King, had left behind.

[P109]
Even Song Ilseom, who had roamed the realm as a wandering martial artist since he was a snot-nosed kid, was surprised.

[P110]
“There’s a road like that?”

[P111]
Ju Hwaran nodded with confidence.

[P112]
“Of course. It’s in my grandfather’s records.”

[P113]
“I spent about a year there myself. But as far as I know…”

[P114]
“It’s in my grandfather’s records.”

[P115]
“Yes, I know. What I’m saying is—”

[P116]
“My grandfather’s records.”

[P117]
“Would you let me finish?”

[P118]
“The Escort King.”

[P119]
“…I believe you. Please continue.”

[P120]
And who was the Escort King? The legend among legends who had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while a hundred thousand Demonic Cultists covered the realm.

[P121]
Ju P. Hwaran had inherited the will of that very P-King. Like the Going Merry on open water, she sailed ahead without a hitch. Before half an hour had passed, she’d planned every leg of our route to Nanman.

[P122]
“Whew. That’s everything for now. Any questions?”

[P123]
*Whoosh!*

[P124]
An arm thick enough to make me suspect it belonged to a Troll shot up.

[P125]
“Yes? Ask away.”

[P126]
Taishan’s face was rigid.

[P127]
“Taishan. Understood nothing after jerky.”

[P128]
“……”

[P129]
“……”

[P130]
*Which bastard brought a kid into a no-kids zone?*

[P131]
I glared at Sama Pyo.

[P132]
“Hey, guardian.”

[P133]
“My apologies.”

[P134]
*Smack.*

[P135]
“Mmph! Mmph!”

[P136]
Sama Pyo clamped a hand over Taishan’s mouth at once, then gave Ju Hwaran a small nod.

[P137]
“My apologies.”

[P138]
“…It’s all right.”

[P139]
Her words were composed, but she couldn’t hide the subdued note in her voice. Given the circumstances, how could she?

[P140]
*Even if it was a political marriage, they were engaged.*

[P141]
Maybe those big-nosed Hollywood bastards, supposedly as cool as ice magic, could shrug off something like that. But the Korea I’d lived in and Murim were both full of Confucian girls and Confucian boys.

[P142]
It was awkward enough for me to watch. How must Ju Hwaran feel?

[P143]
*And I don’t even know what happened between them.*

[P144]
The thought left me feeling strange. Suddenly, the fabric against my skin irritated me, as if someone I couldn’t see were pricking me over and over with a tiny, thin needle.

[P145]
“Captain?”

[P146]
“Hm?”

[P147]
Hyuk Mujin’s voice broke through my thoughts. I didn’t need to turn my head to know the others were staring at me.

[P148]
I pulled myself together and tried to sound casual.

[P149]
“All right. We’ll follow the plan we’ve discussed. Minimal supplies. As for how long we have…”

[P150]
Ju Hwaran answered when I looked at her.

[P151]
“Half a shichen.[^1] Even allowing extra time, that should be enough. We need to arrange the horses and carriages without attracting attention.”

[P152]
“Where should we gather?”

[P153]
“Hmm. What do you think, Great Hero Jin?”

[P154]
This wasn’t a public mission. We had to move as quickly as possible, but discreetly too. To slip away from this crowded area unnoticed, we would first have to split up and choose a second meeting point.

[P155]
“Mount Daebyeol. We’ll meet there.”

[P156]
“Good idea.”

[P157]
Ju Hwaran and the others nodded at the answer I’d arrived at after some thought.

[P158]
[^1]: A shichen is a traditional time unit lasting approximately two hours.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P69]
“But I’ll act as though I don’t. Unfortunately, I’ve already taken a hefty advance, and I can’t afford to pay a penalty ten times that amount.”

[P70]
“That’s a lot simpler than I expected. I like it.”

[P71]
“When I make a contract, I honor it. If I didn’t, I’d never have earned the name Soul-Chasing Guest.”

[P72]
He said it with quiet conviction and pride, then continued matter-of-factly.

[P73]
“Of course, the final decision isn’t mine. It’s my employer’s. Isn’t that right?”

[P74]
Naturally, he wasn’t asking me.

[P75]
Ju Hwaran, the Dagger Hidden Flower, had been silent and deep in thought the whole time. At last, she spoke.

[P76]
“I think you already know my answer. Don’t you?”

[P77]
At the sound of her clear, gentle voice, I let out a quiet laugh. Song Ilseom sighed.

[P78]
“I knew it. Damn it, Nanman.”

[P79]
“I trust I don’t need to remind you of the terms of our contract, Great Hero Song.”

[P80]
Leaving him to groan, Ju Hwaran turned her gaze on me.

[P81]
My face was reflected in her dark blue eyes. They held a mysterious light. From this close, they looked almost…

[P82]
“Great Hero Jin?”

[P83]
“Ah, yes.”

[P84]
*What was that? Did I doze off for a second?*

[P85]
Her voice brought me back to my senses.

[P86]
*No. I can’t do that.*

[P87]
Not now. With what lay ahead, I needed to keep a clear head at all times.

[P88]
I told myself that a few more times, pulled myself together, and spoke as calmly as I could.

[P89]
“Good. There’s something I wanted to ask you. Specifically…”

[P90]
“The fastest route to Nanman and what we’ll need? All right.”

[P91]
“Pardon?”

[P92]
“Was I wrong?”

[P93]
“No. It’s not that.”

[P94]
Quite the opposite. She’d guessed so precisely that she’d startled me.

[P95]
*What the hell? Can she read minds? Is that some kind of mind-reading technique?*

[P96]
I could only blink at her. Ju Hwaran smiled.

[P97]
“There’s no need to be surprised. I’ve been thinking about what I can do to help.”

[P98]
“Oh.”

[P99]
“I’m officially a member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion now. As I said before, I ought to do my share.”

[P100]
*Tap. Tap-tap.*

[P101]
Her pale, rough fingers drummed steadily on the table, a reminder that she was a swordswoman too.

[P102]
“First, as you said, Great Hero Jin, we should keep supplies to a minimum. We won’t need extra clothing, and two days’ worth of dry rations should be enough.”

[P103]
“Dry rations? Please! Anything but that! Taishan will die!”

[P104]
Ju Hwaran quickly added, “And jerky, of course.”

[P105]
“What the hell is his guardian doing? Ah, Young Lady Ju, please go on.”

[P106]
“Of course. Now…”

[P107]
With the interruption dealt with, Ju Hwaran continued without a pause. She covered everything from the supplies we’d need to the fastest route to Nanman.

[P108]
Fortunately, she had traveled there on an escort assignment several years ago. She also knew the terrain and hidden roads in various places from the records her grandfather, the Escort King, had left behind.

[P109]
Even Song Ilseom, who had roamed the realm as a wandering martial artist since he was a snot-nosed kid, was surprised.

[P110]
“There’s a road like that?”

[P111]
Ju Hwaran nodded with confidence.

[P112]
“Of course. It’s in my grandfather’s records.”

[P113]
“I spent about a year there myself. But as far as I know…”

[P114]
“It’s in my grandfather’s records.”

[P115]
“Yes, I know. What I’m saying is—”

[P116]
“My grandfather’s records.”

[P117]
“Would you let me finish?”

[P118]
“The Escort King.”

[P119]
“…I believe you. Please continue.”

[P120]
And who was the Escort King? The legend among legends who had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while a hundred thousand Demonic Cultists covered the realm.

[P121]
Ju P. Hwaran had inherited the will of that very P-King. Like the Going Merry on open water, she sailed ahead without a hitch. Before half an hour had passed, she’d planned every leg of our route to Nanman.

[P122]
“Whew. That’s everything for now. Any questions?”

[P123]
*Whoosh!*

[P124]
An arm thick enough to make me suspect it belonged to a Troll shot up.

[P125]
“Yes? Ask away.”

[P126]
Taishan’s face was rigid.

[P127]
“Taishan. Understood nothing after jerky.”

[P128]
“……”

[P129]
“……”

[P130]
*Which bastard brought a kid into a no-kids zone?*

[P131]
I glared at Sama Pyo.

[P132]
“Hey, guardian.”

[P133]
“My apologies.”

[P134]
*Smack.*

[P135]
“Mmph! Mmph!”

[P136]
Sama Pyo clamped a hand over Taishan’s mouth at once, then gave Ju Hwaran a small nod.

[P137]
“My apologies.”

[P138]
“…It’s all right.”

[P139]
Her words were composed, but she couldn’t hide the subdued note in her voice. Given the circumstances, how could she?

[P140]
*Even if it was a political marriage, they were engaged.*

[P141]
Maybe those big-nosed Hollywood bastards, supposedly as cool as ice magic, could shrug off something like that. But the Korea I’d lived in and Murim were both full of Confucian girls and Confucian boys.

[P142]
It was awkward enough for me to watch. How must Ju Hwaran feel?

[P143]
*And I don’t even know what happened between them.*

[P144]
The thought left me feeling strange. Suddenly, the fabric against my skin irritated me, as if someone I couldn’t see were pricking me over and over with a tiny, thin needle.

[P145]
“Captain?”

[P146]
“Hm?”

[P147]
Hyuk Mujin’s voice broke through my thoughts. I didn’t need to turn my head to know the others were staring at me.

[P148]
I pulled myself together and tried to sound casual.

[P149]
“All right. We’ll follow the plan we’ve discussed. Minimal supplies. As for how long we have…”

[P150]
Ju Hwaran answered when I looked at her.

[P151]
“Half a shichen.[^1] Even allowing extra time, that should be enough. We need to arrange the horses and carriages without attracting attention.”

[P152]
“Where should we gather?”

[P153]
“Hmm. What do you think, Great Hero Jin?”

[P154]
This wasn’t a public mission. We had to move as quickly as possible, but discreetly too. To slip away from this crowded area unnoticed, we would first have to split up and choose a second meeting point.

[P155]
“Mount Daebyeol. We’ll meet there.”

[P156]
“Good idea.”

[P157]
Ju Hwaran and the others nodded at the answer I’d arrived at after some thought.

[^1]: A shichen is a traditional time unit lasting approximately two hours.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

And who was the Escort King? The legend among legends who had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while a hundred thousand Demonic Cultists covered the realm.

[P121]
Ju P. Hwaran had inherited the will of that very P-King. Like the Going Merry on open water, she sailed ahead without a hitch. Before half an hour had passed, she’d planned every leg of our route to Nanman.

[P122]
“Whew. That’s everything for now. Any questions?”

[P123]
*Whoosh!*

[P124]
An arm thick enough to make me suspect it belonged to a Troll shot up.

[P125]
“Yes? Ask away.”

[P126]
Taishan’s face was rigid.

[P127]
“Taishan. Understood nothing after jerky.”

[P128]
“……”

[P129]
“……”

[P130]
*Which bastard brought a kid into a no-kids zone?*

[P131]
I glared at Sama Pyo.

[P132]
“Hey, guardian.”

[P133]
“My apologies.”

[P134]
*Smack.*

[P135]
“Mmph! Mmph!”

[P136]
Sama Pyo clamped a hand over Taishan’s mouth at once, then gave Ju Hwaran a small nod.

[P137]
“My apologies.”

[P138]
“…It’s all right.”

[P139]
Her words were composed, but she couldn’t hide the subdued note in her voice. Given the circumstances, how could she?

[P140]
*Even if it was a political marriage, they were engaged.*

[P141]
Maybe those big-nosed Hollywood bastards, supposedly as cool as ice magic, could shrug off something like that. But the Korea I’d lived in and Murim were both full of Confucian girls and Confucian boys.

[P142]
It was awkward enough for me to watch. How must Ju Hwaran feel?

[P143]
*And I don’t even know what happened between them.*

[P144]
The thought left me feeling strange. Suddenly, the fabric against my skin irritated me, as if someone I couldn’t see were pricking me over and over with a tiny, thin needle.

[P145]
“Captain?”

[P146]
“Hm?”

[P147]
Hyuk Mujin’s voice broke through my thoughts. I didn’t need to turn my head to know the others were staring at me.

[P148]
I pulled myself together and tried to sound casual.

[P149]
“All right. We’ll follow the plan we’ve discussed. Minimal supplies. As for how long we have…”

[P150]
Ju Hwaran answered when I looked at her.

[P151]
“Half a shichen.[^1] Even allowing extra time, that should be enough. We need to arrange the horses and carriages without attracting attention.”

[P152]
“Where should we gather?”

[P153]
“Hmm. What do you think, Great Hero Jin?”

[P154]
This wasn’t a public mission. We had to move as quickly as possible, but discreetly too. To slip away from this crowded area unnoticed, we would first have to split up and choose a second meeting point.

[P155]
“Mount Daebyeol. We’ll meet there.”

[P156]
“Good idea.”

[P157]
Ju Hwaran and the others nodded at the answer I’d arrived at after some thought.

[P158]
[^1]: A shichen is a traditional time unit lasting approximately two hours.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
